source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC-Web -> click "Refresh", and chck that it should refresh.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- "Refresh": refresh the BMC web page (F5) and confirm the UI reloads / session persists. Agent drives the browser refresh and checks the page state.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the page state before/after refresh (session still logged in, data reloaded) so user confirms refresh works.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL identifies browser automation and state comparison, but substitutes browser F5/reload for the source's explicit in-application `Refresh` icon. These can invoke different cache, routing, session and data-fetch paths, so F5 cannot prove the icon function; `risk: none` also ignores unsaved/pending state and duplicate request hazards.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED adds endpoint identity, page scope, pending-state checks, DOM/network readiness and session behavior, but still allows `refresh control or browser reload`. This review retains the classification while requiring the UI Refresh control and recording browser reload only as non-equivalent comparative evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 847/2291 accepts the F5 premise and only defers runtime validation; it never proves the icon exists, is enabled, dispatches its intended request or updates the page.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1010 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 treats page/build/session markers as readiness rather than permanent blockage; ED-35 preserves the source-specified UI control and requires any F5 substitution to record coverage difference; ED-38 requires protected session handling, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC web application's own `Refresh` icon/control is visible, enabled and causes the Project-selected page or widget data to refetch and render a current usable state, without relying on browser F5, losing the authenticated context or issuing an unintended mutation.
original_method: Bind the exact BMC/UI build and approved read-only page; identify the in-app Refresh control; record route, session identity and deterministic server-side data marker; click that control once; verify its specific fetch/activity completes, the marker updates or is freshly revalidated as expected, the route/session remain correct and no form/operation is submitted.
manual_activity: An engineer chooses a safe read-only page/widget, defines the in-app Refresh control and freshness/readiness marker, and confirms session and unsaved-state expectations. Browser automation can perform one control click and collect evidence after approval; ambiguous freshness and final verdict remain engineer-owned.
required_inputs: Immutable BMC identity, trusted web URL/certificate, firmware/UI build and supported browser/version
Exact safe page/widget, account/role, route and stable accessible/DOM selector for the application's Refresh icon; confirmation that it is not browser reload
Authoritative data source and deterministic freshness evidence such as response timestamp, ETag, request ID, sequence/count, last-updated field or approved externally changed value
Expected network request/resource, loading/spinner lifecycle, DOM region, empty/error/stale state and completion timeout
Session/cookie/refresh-token behavior, route persistence, proxy/cache/service-worker policy and whether UI refresh is supposed to bypass or revalidate cache
Inventory of unsaved fields, pending forms/jobs/firmware/power actions and explicit requirement that none is active; protected credentials and screenshot/network redaction
safety_requirements: Use the BMC application's Refresh icon. Do not replace it with F5, Ctrl-R, browser reload or navigation away/back; those test a different mechanism and may conceal a broken UI control.
Choose a read-only page with no unsaved form values or pending power, firmware, reset, credential or configuration operation. Stop if refresh could submit, repeat, cancel or obscure an active action.
Validate the endpoint/certificate/build and protect credentials, cookies and tokens; ensure the post-refresh data still belongs to the same BMC and authenticated account.

Do not accept a spinner, icon animation, unchanged screenshot or HTTP 200 alone. Correlate the control click to the expected request and a server-side freshness/revalidation marker plus completed rendered state.
Do not require a data value to change when the source is legitimately stable; distinguish fresh retrieval of the same value from stale cached content using metadata/request evidence.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL, BMC logs, browser cache or service-worker storage unless the Project explicitly defines that as a separate setup step; cache-clearing changes the test path.

Do not automatically retry a failed or duplicate refresh. Preserve the first click's network/DOM/session/error evidence and stop on unexpected mutation, duplicate request, logout, redirect, wrong endpoint or stuck loading.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, verify BMC/build/account identity, select the approved read-only page, locate the exact UI Refresh control and prove no unsaved or pending operation state exists.
Capture baseline route/session marker, DOM content and server-side freshness metadata; arm browser network/console observation without clearing application data.

After approval, click the in-app control exactly once, correlate its event with the expected read-only request(s), wait for the approved loading/DOM readiness condition and capture new freshness/revalidation metadata and rendered result.

Verify same endpoint/account/route, absence of mutation/duplicate submission/error and expected session behavior; report a stable-but-fresh result distinctly from stale data and do not retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the safe page/widget, UI Refresh selector, expected request and freshness/readiness markers plus stable-value interpretation.
Confirm no pending/unsaved state and define session/cache behavior, timeout and any acceptable visual ambiguity.
Review first-click control/request/data evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Browser automation is appropriate, but F5 is a method mismatch because it bypasses the source icon and may reload the full document rather than trigger the application's data-refresh handler. Before/after appearance alone cannot distinguish fresh data from cache.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a supported browser against the trusted BMC UI, locate the exact in-app Refresh control, capture baseline request/data freshness markers, click once, assert the expected read-only fetch and loading-to-ready DOM transition, and verify no mutation, redirect or session loss.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC web Refresh icon, workable-function criterion, no Script and 5/0-minute estimates remain unmodified; F5 is explicitly not treated as source-equivalent.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Identity/page-state preflight; UI-control binding; baseline freshness metadata; one control click; request-to-DOM readiness correlation; stable-versus-stale interpretation; no-mutation/session verification.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BMC firmware/UI build, page/widget and account role exposing the in-app Refresh control.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/UI build, browser/version, selector, resource/response metadata and cache/service-worker context.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor BMC UI control and page-data contract, not generic browser reload behavior.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes icon functionality and freshness objectively observable while retaining the narrow read-only intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: F5 tests browser document reload, not the app icon; click animation does not prove a fetch; identical values may still be fresh; changed values without endpoint/session identity can be wrong-target data.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Endpoint/build/page, selector, safe state, expected request, freshness/readiness markers, session/cache contract and evidence rules.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A refresh handler can duplicate requests, discard unsaved state, re-trigger pending operations, expose stale cached data or expire the session.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may define the target page/widget, cache contract and build-specific selector. A browser F5 comparison may be added, but if used instead of the UI icon it must record original versus actual mechanism, reason, approval and that the source icon remains unverified.
expected_evidence: BMC endpoint/certificate identity, firmware/UI build, browser/version, redacted account/role and approved page/widget route
Pre-click screenshot/DOM showing the application Refresh control selector, visible/enabled state and absence of unsaved/pending operations
Baseline data plus authoritative freshness metadata, cache/service-worker/proxy context and armed network/console trace
Single click event correlated to expected read-only request/response, request ID/timestamp/ETag/sequence, loading transition and final DOM state
Same route/identity/session, no duplicate/mutating request or error, stable-fresh versus stale conclusion, first-attempt artifact and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently identify the BMC web application's Refresh icon and require its function to work. The exact page and freshness marker are underspecified but can be supplied by Project SPEC without changing the core operation.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The UI control and refresh behavior are identifiable. A safe page, selector, request and freshness/session contract are normal readiness inputs, so the case requires package/user confirmation rather than a permanent block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains browser automation but rejects F5 substitution and `risk: none`; adds control-specific request, freshness and pending-state evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package/user confirmation, safe page, DOM/network readiness and session controls; tightens the method so only the in-app icon satisfies the source and F5 remains non-equivalent.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces acceptance of a browser-reload shortcut with exact icon/event/request/data linkage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a successful browser reload, spinner animation or cached unchanged page from being misreported as a working BMC application Refresh icon.
independent_technical_reasoning: An application refresh handler may issue targeted API reads and preserve route/session state, whereas F5 reconstructs the document and can exercise different caches and authentication paths. Because the source explicitly says click the icon, the control-to-request-to-render chain is the coverage. Freshness must be proven without demanding arbitrary data change, and pending mutable state must be excluded before the click.
